title: Veritide Biosystems — Edge deployment & Terraform notes (draft)
body:
SUMMARY:
This is a working playbook for the proposed Veritide Biosystems private (on-prem / VPC) deployment. Purpose: capture sizing inputs, Terraform module decisions, upgrade/rollback plan, and an architecture Q&A to align with Veritide infra and compliance needs. Draft status: internal review; assumes follow-up network workshop with Veritide infra (week of 2025-02-10).

CONTEXT & ASSUMPTIONS:
- Customer: Veritide Biosystems (bioinformatics SaaS; HIPAA-adjacent data).
- Target environment: single on-prem datacenter for initial rollout (VMware ESXi), with optional cross-site DR to a second colo within 6 months.
- Traffic profile (from sales handoff): 10k inference requests/day for v1, bursty during business hours; expected growth to 50k/day in 12 months. Typical request sizes: 80–512 tokens; 95th percentile latency requirement: 300ms for hosted endpoints.
- Security/compliance: customer requires KMS integration, node-level disk encryption, strict egress controls, and audit logging forwarded to their SIEM.
- Operational model: Redwood provides packaged OVA + Terraform repo to manage control plane connectors and infra-as-code for network, load balancers, and VM pools. Customer ops runs hypervisor and physical network.

HIGH-LEVEL ARCHITECTURE:
- Control plane (Redwood-managed control plane in customer VPC or customer-managed proxy): lightweight control connector (k8s-agnostic) runs in customer network to register compute pool and push policies.
- Inference plane: Kubernetes (EKS-on-prem / K8s distro) or VM-based runtime depending on customer preference. For Veritide we recommend VM pool backed by GPU nodes in their VMware cluster for simplicity with existing tooling.
- Storage: NFS for model artifacts + encrypted block storage for local KV cache snapshots.
- Network: internal LB (HAProxy/MetalLB) distributing requests to replica pools; egress gateway for telemetry and license checks (whitelisted).

SIZING (initial / baseline):
- Workload assumptions: 50 concurrent active requests at peak, average token generation 200, model: Llama-2-13B (quantized int8) or comparable 13–14B family.
- Recommended node plan (on-prem):
  - GPU nodes: 3 x A10G-equivalent (24GB) for model serving (each with 8 vCPU, 64GB RAM). This supports continuous batching and KV cache for 50 concurrent requests with headroom.
  - CPU nodes: 2 x 16vCPU, 64GB (for control/sidecar tasks, pre/post-processing, batching aggregator).
  - Storage: 2TB encrypted block storage for model cache + 5TB NFS for artifacts and backups.
- Cost/efficiency note: if Veritide approves quantized 4-bit models and more aggressive batching, GPU count can be reduced to 2 for non-peak workloads.

CAPACITY CALCULATION (back-of-envelope):
- Throughput per A10G for quantized 13B with our runtime: ~8 tokens/ms peak (approx). For 200 tokens average, generation time ~25ms per request pure compute. With overheads (network, batching windows), plan for 75–120ms per request.
- Then 50 concurrent -> sustained token generation rate of ~10k tokens/s -> GPUs above meet headroom with batching.

TERRAFORM MODULE NOTES (repo: terraform/veritide-edge):
- Module layout: modules/network, modules/vm_pool, modules/storage, modules/connector. Keep modules minimal and parameterized for customer overrides.
- Example variable decisions to surface to Veritide:
  - gp_node_count (default 3)
  - gp_instance_profile (A10G|A100-small)
  - storage_encryption (bool)
  - siem_forwarding_endpoint (string)
  - control_connector_mode (pull|push)
- Recommended module patterns:
  - Use separate state files per module group (network-state.tfstate, compute-state.tfstate) to reduce blast radius during upgrades.
  - Lock state with remote backend (consul or remote s3) — if customer can't provide, recommend remote agent-based state manager.
  - Provide sample varfile: veritide.tfvars.example with prefilled values and comments.
- Terraform snippet (example usage):
  module "gp_pool" {
    source = "../../modules/vm_pool"
    gp_node_count = var.gp_node_count
    gp_instance_profile = var.gp_instance_profile
    network_segment = module.network.segment_id
  }

UPGRADE & ROLLBACK PLAN (high level):
- Goal: non-disruptive model runtime and control connector updates.
- Phased plan:
  1) Canary: deploy new runtime to 1 GPU node, route 1–2% of traffic, monitor latency and error rates for 1 hour.
  2) Gradual rollout: increase to 25% over 30m, 50% over 30m, full if no regressions.
  3) Rollback: Terraform plan will create replacement nodes; maintain previous AMI/image and model artifact set. If latency or error rate exceeds threshold, shift traffic back to previous pool and destroy canary nodes.
- Terraform strategy for upgrades:
  - Avoid in-place replacement of all GPUs at once: use count-based or lifecycle create_before_destroy patterns for gp_pool.
  - Keep model artifacts tagged by semantic version and ensure runtime can load multi-version models concurrently (side-by-side).

OPERATIONAL RUNBOOK (concise):
- Day 0: preflight checklist (network ACLs, proxy egress whitelist, KMS access, ESXi host labeling, datastore capacity check).
- Day 1: Provision network + control connector using terraform apply -var-file=veritide.tfvars; verify registration in Redwood Console (test heartbeat).
- Smoke tests: run 100 synthetic requests across 3 models (search, chat, embeddings). Validate token accounting and latency SLA.
- Monitoring: push metrics to customer Prometheus/Datadog with tags: env=veritide, team=platform, model=13b-q8.

ARCHITECTURE Q&A (notes from last call with Veritide ops):
- Q: Can we use customer's KMS?
  A: Yes. We will integrate via CMK in customer VPC; Terraform uses provider for key grant and resource access. Requires service account with Encrypt/Decrypt.
- Q: Is cross-site replication required now?
  A: Not initially; Veritide prefers single-site with RTO 4h. We recommend planning for second site in quarter 2 with async model sync.
- Q: Are GPUs on shared cluster or reserved?
  A: Veritide prefers reserved GPU hosts in a dedicated cluster for isolation; we recommend node pool tagging and tenant isolation via network segmentation.
- Open question: exact SIEM endpoint and log format (CEF vs JSON). Action: Rohit to confirm with Veritide security by 2025-02-12.

SECURITY & COMPLIANCE NOTES:
- Encrypt all at-rest volumes with customer KMS.
- Minimize egress: only allow telemetry endpoints. Use VPC proxy for license checks.
- Audit: enable detailed audit logging on connector and transfer logs to SIEM; maintain 90-day retention by default, extendable on request.

TESTING & ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (proposed):
- Functional: all Redwood endpoints respond and models load correctly under 1% error rate during 1-hour soak at peak expected traffic.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for chat endpoint under expected load (as measured by our synthetic test harness).
- Security: KMS usage verified and logs flowing to SIEM; no outbound ports open beyond whitelisted.

NEXT STEPS / ACTION ITEMS:
- Schedule network deep-dive with Veritide infra (Ava/Rohit) — target 2025-02-10.
- Finalize terraform varfile and seed public AMI images (Ava) — target 2025-02-17.
- Security confirmation for SIEM format (Rohit) — target 2025-02-12.
- Provide compact runbook PDF for customer ops (Lena) — target 2025-02-21.

NOTES / THREADS / REFERENCES:
- Related internal playbook: terraform/modules/edge-patterns (link in repo).
- Prior customer reference: internal notes from Aurora Financial on onprem sizing (see CONFLUENCE link).

---
This doc is iterative — expect follow-ups that update the gp_node_count calculations and Terraform module params after the network deep-dive. Marked as draft for review.
